description.summary: the compositor's channel to its desktop shell

protocol.description:
What passes between perspicax and perspicax-shell that no standard protocol carries: the person asked for a menu or a pie, the config changed, the session should end, the keyboard's layouts and which is in use.
Everything else the shell does, it does as any other client would. Its wallpaper, panel and menus are layer-shell surfaces, its taskbar speaks wlr-foreign-toplevel-management and its pager ext-workspace. That keeps this protocol small, and every piece of the shell replaceable by a program that speaks only the standard ones.
The global is privileged: the compositor offers it only to the programs its [protocols] shell rule admits, and withdraws it, with finished, from a client a reload no longer admits. While the session is locked the compositor sends nothing and ignores every request.

interface.name: perspicax_shell_v1

description.summary: a shell's binding to the compositor

interface.description: Bound once by a shell. Several shells may bind it; each is told the same things.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The shell is done with this object. Nothing more is sent on it.

request.name: exit_session
request.description: The person chose to log out. The compositor ends the session, as Ctrl+Alt+Backspace does, taking every client with it.

event.name: start_menu

description.summary: the person asked for the start menu

event.description:
A binding asked for the start menu: a tap of the Logo key, say. A shell shows its start menu on this monitor, or hides it if it is already showing, as a second tap does on Plasma.
The output is the monitor under the pointer, or null if this client has not bound that monitor's wl_output.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the monitor to show it on

event.name: root_menu

description.summary: the person asked for the root menu

event.description:
A binding asked for the root menu, the desktop's own menu that a right-click on the wallpaper also opens. A shell shows it at x, y, in logical pixels from the monitor's top-left corner, or hides it if it is already showing.
The position is where the pointer is, which a shell cannot see for itself while the pointer is over another client's window.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the monitor the pointer is on

event.name: reconfigure
event.description: The person saved a config file whose shell settings differ from the ones this shell started with. A shell reads the file again and applies it in place.

event.name: finished
event.description: This client is no longer admitted: a reload changed the rule. The compositor sends nothing more and ignores every request; the shell should destroy the object.

request.name: set_layout
request.description: The person chose a layout on the shell: clicked its indicator, say. The compositor switches the keyboard to layout index, counted from 0 in the order the layout events named them. An index past the last is ignored.

event.name: layout
event.description: Sent for each of the keyboard's layouts in order, from index 0, when the object is bound and again whenever the keymap changes, then layouts_done.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: xkb's name for it, as English (US)

arg.name: short
arg.summary: a label for a panel, as US

event.name: layouts_done
event.description: The layout events since the last layouts_done are the keyboard's layouts now, and replace any named before.

event.name: active_layout
event.description: Sent after layouts_done, and whenever the layout in use changes.

arg.name: index
arg.summary: the layout in use, counted from 0

event.name: pie_menu

description.summary: the person asked for a pie menu

event.description:
A binding asked for the pie menu of this name, one of the config's [shell.pie.menus]. A shell shows it centred at x, y, in logical pixels from the monitor's top-left corner, or hides it if that pie is the one showing; another pie showing gives way to it.
The position is where the pointer is, which a shell cannot see for itself while the pointer is over another client's window.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the monitor the pointer is on
